entries.title: II Corinthians 3:14
segments: The same veil remaineth.  The language is figurative: the veil which remained was the belief of the hardened Jewish heart in the sacredness of the old covenant (of the law), which prevented the realization that it had passed away under the new covenant in Christ.

entries.title: II Corinthians 3:15
segments: A veil lieth upon their heart. Many scholars see in this passage a reference to the Jewish custom of covering the head with a four-cornered veil called the tallith, when they were in the synagogue.  The tallith did not cover the eyes but hung down over the breast.
